definition: A future relative 0-100 indicator of evidence for market interest and opportunity under a declared provider, geography, language, network, and time window. It is not a forecast or validation claim.
fixed_principles: Only validated Phase 2A real-external-provider observations and provenance-valid upstream artifacts may be inputs.
Evidence availability and evidence value are distinct; missing evidence never becomes zero demand.
Evidence breadth affects confidence, not Demand Potential.
Search attention is an attention proxy, not sales demand.
Advertiser activity is an advertiser-market signal, not consumer demand.
Overlapping query volumes are never summed as independent consumers.
Baseline category queries provide context only and never contribute directly as concept-specific demand evidence.
Scores, bands, and rankings remain prohibited until pilot calibration is completed and a subsequent executable methodology artifact is approved.
All contributing queries, observations, transformations, exclusions, and hashes must remain explainable and reproducible.
No synthetic or fixture observation may be represented as real market evidence.

dimensions.meaning: Relative level of observed search attention for reviewed concept attributes within a comparable evidence scope.
permitted_inputs: baseline category observations for context only
exclusions: baseline category volume as a direct score contributor

dimensions.meaning: Direction and persistence of comparable monthly search activity for reviewed concept attributes.
Observed advertiser competition and bid activity, interpreted only as an advertiser-market signal.
permitted_inputs: provider currency and scope metadata when required
exclusions: advertiser activity interpreted as consumer demand
invented numeric mappings from missing fields
missing bid or competition data treated as zero

baseline_category_treatment: Baseline category queries are context controls. They may support a pilot-calibrated category-relative interpretation only when provider, geography, language, network, and time window match. They never enter the v1 score as direct concept-specific query contributions and may not dominate through larger volume.

missing_data_semantics.observed_zero: An explicit numeric zero returned by the provider is observed evidence and may be used as zero.
missing_data_semantics.no_data: The provider returned no usable metric; the value is missing and is never converted to zero.
missing_data_semantics.suppressed: The provider withheld a metric, including possible privacy or low-volume suppression; the value is missing and is never converted to zero.
missing_data_semantics.unavailable: The metric is unavailable for the requested scope; the value is missing and is never converted to zero.
missing_data_semantics.provider_error: Collection failed at the provider; no demand value may be inferred.
missing_data_semantics.permission_denied: Access was refused; no demand value may be inferred.

confidence_components.rule: Measure usable non-category signal-type coverage with each type counted once; query count cannot increase credit.
Measure valid comparable monthly coverage; the exact minimum and window remain pilot-calibration-dependent.
Distinguish terminal provider outcomes from provider or permission failures without treating no_data as numeric evidence.
Require consistent provider methodology, geography, language, network, time window, and collection scope.
One real provider receives partial rather than full credit. Lack of a second provider alone does not make an otherwise sufficient result unreportable.
All hashes, IDs, query text, evidence states, attribute pointers, and concept/refinement lineage must validate; failure is fail-closed.

single_provider_source_breadth_rule: A single independently operated real provider receives partial source-breadth credit. Reportability is assessed across all confidence components and must not fail solely because a second provider is absent.

pilot_calibration_parameters.conceptual_approach: Evaluate log-transformed search attention and robust cohort normalization, including proposed P10/P90 behavior, only after inspecting real provider distributions.
Test whether category baselines are semantically and statistically stable enough for a bounded context adjustment; never permit direct category contribution.
Inspect provider grouping and close variants before fixing attribution. One provider result cluster must never be duplicated across queries.
Determine the minimum usable month count from actual returned histories; missing months remain missing.
Evaluate recent-versus-prior windows and persistence behavior against actual provider granularity before selecting constants.
Inspect returned bid coverage, currency, skew, and missingness before selecting a log or percentile normalization.
Set final coverage, confidence, and comparability gates only after real provider behavior is observed; failures and missing values may not be relaxed into zeros.

provenance_requirements: Every contributing metric must resolve to a validated normalized Phase 2A observation and immutable raw response.
Every observation must resolve through reviewed query ID, exact query text, attribute reference, concept ID, refinement SHA-256, and Creative Refinement v2 artifact SHA-256.
Every calculation must record methodology ID, methodology artifact SHA-256, input artifact hashes, normalization cohort hash, scope, timestamp, exclusions, and contributing observation IDs.
Synthetic, fixture, ambiguous, ineligible, stale, altered, or provenance-invalid inputs are prohibited.
versioning_policy: This preimplementation artifact is immutable and non-executable.
Pilot-calibrated constants require a new immutable methodology artifact and identifier before scoring is permitted.
Changes to dimensions, weights, formulas, overlap handling, missing-data semantics, confidence logic, bands, or reportability gates require a new methodology version.
Historical result artifacts must retain the exact methodology artifact SHA-256 and must never be silently recalculated.
unresolved_questions: Whether Google Ads Basic access returns sufficient metrics for the reviewed niche queries.
How Google Ads groups or omits close variants for these specific queries.
Whether broad category phrases are stable and meaningful context controls.
The returned month count, missing-month behavior, and appropriate momentum window.
Bid coverage, currency consistency, and suitable robust normalization.
Final confidence and reportability thresholds after observing real suppression and failure rates.
Which independent second source can add defensible source breadth in a future phase.
When provenance-backed real trend intelligence and brand relevance become eligible future dimensions.
